title: LE10: original mid-plane line support
summary: Reproduce the original SimScale/NAFEMS LE10 support split with a reproducible imported Hex20 mesh, then check signed stress, refinement and force balance.

steps.title: Start original NAFEMS LE10
steps.explain: Reproduce the original SimScale/NAFEMS thick elliptic plate problem. In-plane motion is held on the outer curved face; vertical motion is held only on its mid-plane line. The signed reference stress is −5.38 MPa.

steps.title: Units and compression
steps.explain: Use metres, newtons and MPa. Positive pressure acts into the top surface; compressive stress is negative.

steps.title: Elastic steel
steps.explain: Use the published isotropic material: E = 210 GPa and ν = 0.3. This static problem needs no thermal or inertial properties.

doIt.name: steel
doIt.source: NAFEMS LE10 / SimScale: isotropic E=210 GPa, nu=0.3

steps.title: Import the reproducible curved Hex20 mesh
steps.explain: The two ellipses have semi-axes (2, 1) m and (3.25, 2.75) m; thickness is 0.6 m. Import the authored 6 × 6 × 6 quadratic mesh: 1225 nodes and 216 Hex20 cells. The exact named outer-midline Set contains 13 nodes at z = 0.3 m. Imported order 1 retains the authored Hex20 connectivity; it does not turn these into linear cells. This source is generated by tools/generate-le10-original.mjs through the registered mesher, INP exporter and converter, with a SHA-256 of the complete source deck including the support Set.

fields.support: 13 outer mid-plane nodes; other outer nodes free in z

steps.title: Assign the material
steps.explain: Imported source groups are analysis targets. Assign steel to the plate Body, preserving all face and node Sets.

steps.title: Mirror the x cut
steps.explain: Remove ux only at x = 0. Tangential motion, including bending in z, remains free.

steps.title: Mirror the y cut
steps.explain: Remove uy only at y = 0. Point D is the upper inner corner on this cut: (2, 0, 0.6) m.

steps.title: Hold the outer face in plane
steps.explain: Fix only ux and uy over the entire outer curved face. Do not add uz here: the original benchmark permits the upper and lower outer edges to move vertically.

steps.title: Hold only the outer mid-plane line in z
steps.explain: Fix uz on plate.nset_outer-midline only. Its 13 nodes lie on the outer ellipse at z = 0.3 m. The other 120 outer-face nodes keep their z freedom. This support split is the essential difference from the separate ESRD full-face variant.

steps.title: Press the upper surface
steps.explain: Apply 1 MPa down onto z = 0.6 m. The bottom surface is unloaded. The total vertical reaction should balance approximately 5.449 MN.

steps.title: Define the original static step
steps.explain: Activate both reflection constraints, the outer in-plane support, the mid-plane vertical support and the top pressure. Every constraint is explicit and enters the Journal.

steps.title: Solve and inspect point D
steps.explain: The quadratic mesh gives σyy(D) ≈ −5.3803 MPa against the unchanged independent −5.38 MPa reference. Probe component 1 at [2 m, 0 m, 0.6 m]; neither von Mises nor the mid-plane stress answers this benchmark question. Mesh import and geometry certification can take longer than the linear solve.

steps.title: Show the requested stress component
steps.explain: Show σyy, component 1, in MPa on the solved plate. This view action changes neither the Model nor the Journal.

steps.title: Fit the plate
steps.explain: Fit the entire plate. Inspect the two symmetry cuts and the split outer support, then compare the local stress with global force balance.

steps.title: Original supports, reference and refinement
steps.explain: A support definition, signed component and probe location are part of the physical problem.
steps.theory:
The original benchmark asks for $\sigma_{yy}(D)$ at $D=(2,0,0.6)\,\mathrm m$, with independent reference **−5.38 MPa**. Our uniform quadratic refinements give **−5.65287 MPa** (4 × 4 × 2), **−5.40449 MPa** (4 × 4 × 4) and **−5.38031 MPa** (6 × 6 × 6). The absolute errors decrease; the final relative error is about **0.0057%**. The automated check solves all three meshes, checks the unchanged published reference and verifies force equilibrium. These are discrete point-stress refinements, not a claim of a formal global convergence rate for a singular line support.

Use `query.probe` with `step: "static"`, `field: "stress"`, `component: 1`, `at: ["2 m", "0 m", "0.6 m"]`. This is interpolated recovered nodal stress, not a raw Gauss-point value. Check the vertical reaction (about **5.449 MN**) as well. The mid-plane rim has essentially zero uz, while the upper and lower outer edges move vertically by about **−9.77 μm** and **−8.65 μm**. Holding the entire outer face in z would remove these motions and change the problem.

The separate **LE10 full-face support variant** fixes ux, uy and uz over the whole outer face and uses ESRD’s **−5.25 MPa** reference. Both workflows are useful; their supports and references must stay paired. The imported source deck and reproducible generator retain the named mid-plane Set in the SHA-256 provenance.

**Other solvers:** the quadratic solid is comparable to Abaqus C3D20, Ansys SOLID186 and a 20-node Nastran CHEXA. Reflection constraints remove the normal component; the outer support uses in-plane SPCs and a separate vertical line SPC. Compare the actual constraints and stress recovery, not only the element name.

Sources: [SimScale: thick plate under pressure](https://www.simscale.com/docs/validation-cases/thick-plate-under-pressure/); [ESRD standard NAFEMS benchmark guide, pp. 29–31](https://www.esrd.com/wp-content/uploads/dlm_uploads/Benchmarks-Guide-Standard-NAFEMS-Benchmarks-Linear-Elastic-Tests.pdf). This is a re-authored workflow using FEM Lab Commands; no vendor tutorial is embedded.
